chunking_profile.strategy: respect plant section and page boundaries, then fixed-token child chunks
chunking_profile.token_unit_contract: Provider-neutral regex units: Unicode word sequences or individual non-whitespace punctuation; these are deterministic portable units, not Gemini tokenizer counts.
chunking_profile.promotion_scope: Four bounded cross-volume samples plus four production candidates: Atropa belladonna PDF pages 35-36, Piper nigrum reviewed ranges on PDF pages 293-296, Polygala senega reviewed ranges on PDF pages 101-102, and Laminaria hyperborea reviewed ranges on PDF pages 315-316; no full-volume promotion is implied.
chunking_profile.rationale: The four-volume samples established a portable contract without claiming universal superiority. Atropa showed a concrete rank-1 gain over whole pages. Piper and Polygala passed the answer/refusal gates; Laminaria required deterministic German lexical expansion, parent collapse and an exact source-term gate. All remain bounded evidence packages, not proof of universal profile superiority.

canonical_chunk_contract.rule: The source chunk export is canonical; every vector index is disposable and rebuildable.

migration_policy.model_or_dimension_or_prompt_change: create a new vector_space_id and rebuild all vectors in that space
migration_policy.portable_export: JSONL is required; Parquet with fixed-size-list vectors may be added for large exports.

retrieval_policy.fusion: For the current bounded toxicology route: cosine + 0.08 * deterministic lexical coverage; exact book-term evidence still authorizes or refuses the answer.
retrieval_policy.rerank_gate: Every answer still requires page-linked book evidence; vector proximity alone never authorizes an answer.
retrieval_policy.chunking_evaluation: One bounded sample from each volume and four production candidates pass the portable 512/100 contract. Atropa demonstrates a real rank-1 gain; Piper demonstrates clean related-taxon range exclusion; Polygala demonstrates bilingual Senegin retrieval; Laminaria demonstrates that dense same-taxon pages require deterministic German term expansion and parent collapse. Strychnos and Laminaria show why hybrid term gating remains necessary. Expansion continues only through bounded, source-checked batches.
retrieval_policy.parent_page_collapse: After channel fusion and before final top-k, retain the maximum hybrid score per parent page so duplicated overlap does not crowd out other evidence.
